column1: # THE SCHMUL SIDE, SEARCHED AT LAST — AND THE 1874 INDEX NAMES SIX PEOPLE, NOT FOUR.
# genealogiawarchiwach.pl, searched 27 September 2026. Scan-mode search on SCHMUL, then filtered
# to the town of SZUBIN. Controls: the unfiltered search reproduces the archive's recorded figure
# exactly — "Found 119 scans from 34 teams, 104 units" — so the instrument is the one row 265 meant.
field
# ---------------- FIRST, A CORRECTION TO THE SCALE OF THE OPPORTUNITY ----------------
*** THE 119 SCANS ARE NOT FRIEDERICA'S TOWN. THEY ARE A DIFFERENT SCHMUL POPULATION. ***
column2: row 265 records that the surname is "indexed ONE HUNDRED AND NINETEEN TIMES across 104 units... THE SCHMUL SIDE IS OPEN TO A NAME SEARCH IN A WAY THE LEIBHOLZ SIDE IS NOT." The first half is exactly right. THE SECOND HALF OVERSTATES WHAT IS AVAILABLE AT SZUBIN. Filtering the same search to the town gives "Found 2 SCANS from 2 teams, 3 units".

column1: where the 119 actually are
column2: WĄBRZEŹNO 43 — the single largest concentration, and an Urząd Stanu Cywilnego of its own — with 60 of the scans held at the Archiwum Państwowe w Toruniu rather than Bydgoszcz. Then Bydgoszcz 12, Grudziądz 5, Inowrocław 4. Wąbrzeźno is about a hundred kilometres north of Szubin. THEY ARE PROBABLY ANOTHER FAMILY, and nothing joins them to Friederica.

column1: so the lane is narrow and not wide, and it is still worth walking
column2: two scans at Szubin, and one of them is the document this archive already holds. WHAT IT GIVES IS BELOW, AND IT IS A GENERATION.

column1: # ---------------- *** THE 1874 MARRIAGE INDEX NAMES SIX PEOPLE *** ----------------
the index line, verbatim
column2: USC Szubin Miasto, Akta małżeństw, sygn. 141, 1874: "powiązane indeksy: SALLY LEIBHOLZ, JACOB LEIBHOLZ, PHILIPINE POLLNOW, FRIEDERICA SCHMUL, JUDA SCHMUL, JETTE MACHOT".

column1: *** FRIEDERICA SCHMUL'S PARENTS ARE JUDA SCHMUL AND JETTE MACHOT ***
column2: THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER HELD EITHER NAME. It read the entry at the image on 22 September and took from it the groom's side — Sally, his father Jacob, his mother née Pollnow — and the bride's own name, and stopped. THE INDEX CARRIES THE BRIDE'S PARENTS TOO. A Prussian marriage entry names the parents of both parties, which this archive has said repeatedly about other people's marriage records and did not apply to the one in its own hands.

column1: what that is worth
column2: FRIEDERICA SCHMUL WAS BORN AND LIVING AT SZUBIN AND WAS ABOUT TWENTY IN NOVEMBER 1874, so born about 1854. Her parents are therefore a couple at Szubin in the 1850s, and MACHOT is a surname this archive has never searched anywhere.

column1: *** AND A DISCREPANCY WITH A PUBLISHED FINDING, WHICH IS NOT RESOLVED HERE ***
column2: THE INDEX SAYS "PHILIPINE POLLNOW". THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED "WILHELMINE GEB. POLLNOW", read at the image on 22 September, and treated her as a new great-great-grandmother — she is on the front-page chart and in the register. PHILIPINE AND WILHELMINE ARE NOT THE SAME NAME.

column1: how to settle it, and it is not by preferring one source
column2: both are readings of the same Kurrent hand: the archive's own from the scan, the portal's from a volunteer indexer working the same scan. NEITHER IS AUTHORITATIVE OVER THE OTHER. The entry must be re-read at the image with this specific question in front of the reader, because a name read once without an alternative in mind is not a name read against one. UNTIL THEN THE ARCHIVE SHOULD NOT QUIETLY KEEP EITHER.

column1: # ---------------- *** AND A CANDIDATE SIBLING FOR FRIEDERICA *** ----------------
*** ABRAHAM SCHMUL, BORN SZUBIN 1846, DIED KORONOWO 1904 ***
column2: the second Szubin scan, from the indexed-persons layer: "Abraham Schmul 1846-1904 Szubin · birth place SZUBIN · birth year 1846 · death place KORONOWO · death year 1904 · father names JULIUSZ · mother names JETTE · mother last name (maiden name) MUSCHLL".

column1: why he is a candidate and not a fact
column2: FOR: born at Szubin, the same small town, eight years before Friederica; the right generation exactly; AND HIS MOTHER IS A JETTE, which is the forename the 1874 index gives Friederica's mother. MUSCHLL and MACHOT are close enough in a Kurrent hand to be one name read twice. AGAINST: his father is JULIUSZ and hers is JUDA. Those are different names, though both are the kind an indexer renders freely — Juda, Judas, Julius, Juliusz all sit on one another in these registers.

column1: what would settle it
column2: his own birth entry at Szubin in 1846, which names his parents in the registrar's hand rather than an indexer's, and Friederica's birth entry about 1854. BOTH PREDATE PRUSSIAN CIVIL REGISTRATION, which began on 1 October 1874 — so these are JEWISH CONGREGATIONAL REGISTERS, and row 266's letter to Bydgoszcz about exactly those books is the outstanding question they depend on.

column1: and a death place that is new
column2: KORONOWO, 1904, about forty kilometres north of Szubin. If he is her brother, the family did not stay put.

column1: # ---------------- ONE INSTRUMENT TESTED AND NOT USABLE ----------------
the Diário da República historical search was tried and did NOT answer
column2: diariodarepublica.pt was opened to test whether a colonial civil servant's appointment could be found in the official gazette, which would confirm the Torre do Tombo personnel file. A search on the name returned nothing — AND SO DID A CONTROL ON THE BARE SURNAME, with an empty page body. THE SEARCH DID NOT RUN. Recorded as untested rather than as a negative, because a zero from an instrument that was not answering is the fault this archive has spent a week learning to refuse.
